title: Engine Wang tile autotile primitive — `engine/render/autotile/` resolver + family registry + change-event subscription
intent: User aspirational feature 2026-05-28: 'wang tiles для создания карт с автотайлингом'. Wang-tile-based autotiling for grid games — for each tile family ('soft-block', 'hard-block', 'floor'), the project registers 16 mesh variants (one per N/E/S/W edge-bitmask of same-family neighbours). The engine resolver computes each cell's bitmask + picks the matching variant. Re-resolves on family-change events (block destroyed, block spawned). Generic — any grid-based game gets it for free. First consumer: Kaboom Crew arenas (paired story GDP-2026-05-28-004).
rationale: Source: `docs/game-design/wang-tile-autotile-design.md` (this batch) + memory [project-visual-fidelity-evolution]. After tile-mesh variety lands (GDP-2026-05-28-003), the SELECTION logic becomes the next problem — random selection produces visual noise; neighbour-aware selection produces 'connected wall' read. Wang tiles are the textbook primitive for this. Engine module per CLAUDE.md (reusable across any grid game — Kaboom now, RPG-tile-map sample later, Beacon-World eventually).
acceptanceHints: READ FIRST: `docs/game-design/wang-tile-autotile-design.md` — the canonical schema + resolver behaviour + first-consumer mapping all live there.
DIRECTORY: NEW `engine/render/autotile/`.
SCHEMA FILES (under `schemas/components/`):
wang-tile.schema.json — WangTile component { familyName: string, currentVariantIndex?: number, currentMeshEntityId?: EntityId }
wang-tile-family.schema.json — WangTileFamily { name, variants: WangTileVariant[16], defaults? }
wang-tile-variant.schema.json — { meshKey, materialOverrides?, rotationY?, mirrorX? }
FAMILY REGISTRY (engine/render/autotile/family-registry.ts):
registerWangTileFamily(family: WangTileFamily): void — throws on duplicate name. Validates variants.length === 16.
getWangTileFamily(name: string): WangTileFamily | undefined
listWangTileFamilies(): string[]
RESOLVER (engine/render/autotile/wang-tile-resolver-system.ts):
System runs on scene load — for every WangTile entity, compute bitmask from 4 neighbours + index into family.variants + spawn variant mesh + apply rotation/mirror.
Subscribes to family-membership change events. Per event: re-resolve the changed cell + its 4 cardinal neighbours (their bitmasks may have flipped).
Old variant mesh entity disposed; new variant mesh entity spawned + child-parented to the WangTile cell entity.
BITMASK ENCODING (matches design doc §3): bit3=N, bit2=E, bit1=S, bit0=W. Same-family neighbour → set bit. Variants[0..15] indexed by bitmask.
DOCTOR INTEGRATION: 'Wang tile families: N registered ([names]). Active wang-tile cells: M.' Warning if any family is missing required variants.

EVENT SUBSCRIPTION: the resolver needs to know when a cell's family-membership changes. Generic approach: the resolver subscribes to ECS component-change events for components tagged 'family-membership'. Projects use their existing block-spawn / block-destroy systems; they just write the standard component on cell entities, and any ADD/REMOVE of that component triggers the resolver. Engine doesn't need to know about specific game components.

TEST FIXTURE: tests/fixtures/autotile/ — a 3×3 grid with a procedural test family 'test-fam' that has 16 distinguishable variants (each variant's mesh has the bitmask number printed on it as vertex colour). Unit tests assert resolver picks variants[5] for the cell with N+W neighbours, variants[15] for fully-surrounded, etc.
PROCEDURAL VARIANT AUTHORING (recommended path for first consumer):

Engine exposes a registerProceduralWangFamily helper: project provides one builder function `buildVariant(index: number) => BufferGeometry`; the helper auto-creates the 16-variant family. The builder reads the bitmask to decide bevel/corner detail.
E.g. soft-block builder: variant 0 (isolated) → smaller box with bigger bevels (looks like 'a brick'); variant 15 (surrounded) → bigger box with flat sides (looks like 'wall filler').
PERFORMANCE BUDGET: full resolve on scene load is O(cells). 17×17 arena = 289 cells, ~1ms total. Per-event re-resolve = 5 cells × ~3μs each = 15μs. Negligible steady-state cost.
UNIT TESTS:
Family registry: register + lookup + list + duplicate-name error.
Bitmask computation: known neighbourhood → correct bitmask.
resolveAt(): writes WangTile.currentVariantIndex + spawns variant mesh.
resolveAll(): walks every WangTile entity in scene.
Family-change event: cell adds family-component → resolver re-runs for cell + 4 neighbours.
Schema validation: malformed family (15 variants instead of 16) rejected.
OUT OF SCOPE:
Multi-color Wang tiles (3+ tile types matching). Binary per family stays.
Per-corner Wang encoding (uses 4-edge instead).
Per-cell random sub-variant within a Wang index (defer to playtest).
Diagonal-adjacency Wang tiles. 4-cardinal only.
3D Wang tiles (top+bottom adjacency).
In-game Wang tile editor UI.
